scope: Read-only audit. No tracked file is modified, no CT case is mapped, no manifest stage status is changed, no verdict is promoted. Every proposal below is a proposal.

method.counted_as_executed: a stage is called executed only when a named workspace test runs it on the case's own artifact. Fixture existence, a manifest string, a hand-written Rust event test and a report transcript do not count.

source probes with target/debug/qcorec, verified current (no .rs file newer than the binary)

claims_exceeding_executed_evidence.subject: all 9 native-mode cases (CT01,CT12,CT13,CT14,CT15,CT16,CT20,CT37,CT50)
claims_exceeding_executed_evidence.finding: No assertion targets a CFG artifact. The sequential resource CFG is provably NOT run: compile_task_source (crates/qcore-verification/src/driver.rs:1100-1212) never calls synthesize_semantics or check_whole_program, and returns reference_observation: None. The claim is defensible only under the unstated reading 'cfg' = the task IR's blocks/terminators, which is exercised transitively by check_task_module/emit_task_c11 but never independently checked.
claims_exceeding_executed_evidence.severity: stage name is ambiguous and unevidenced
claims_exceeding_executed_evidence.proposed_repair: retire the single `cfg` stage; replace with `task_lowering`, `task_ledger_check` and `sequential_whole_program` (the last `not_applicable` for every current mapped case)

claims_exceeding_executed_evidence.subject: CT02, CT19
claims_exceeding_executed_evidence.finding: Both reject at Q600 in qcore_core::task_execution::check_task_module -- the task ledger, which runs AFTER elaboration and after lower_source_tasks. The two-stage label makes a deep ledger rejection indistinguishable from a shallow Q013 name-resolution rejection. Verified: CT02 expects Q600 'not an initialized owned buffer', CT19 expects Q600 'ScopeBusy'.
claims_exceeding_executed_evidence.severity: under-records executed depth; hides reject-reason provenance
claims_exceeding_executed_evidence.proposed_repair: record task_lowering and task_ledger_check as separately executed stages and pin the rejecting pass

claims_exceeding_executed_evidence.subject: all 9 native-mode cases
claims_exceeding_executed_evidence.finding: The runners are Linux-gated: on a non-Linux host every run_native_* helper returns after unsupported_target() and prints 'unexecuted on this host'. reference_execution, cfg and native_backend then do not execute, yet the manifest field still reads 'executed'. The manifest `note` acknowledges the scoping in prose; the machine-readable field a summarizer consumes does not.
claims_exceeding_executed_evidence.severity: machine-readable field overstates on non-Linux hosts
claims_exceeding_executed_evidence.proposed_repair: make host_gate a first-class per-stage field and have the summarizer report executed_on(host)

claims_exceeding_executed_evidence.subject: CT14, CT16, CT20, CT37, CT50
claims_exceeding_executed_evidence.manifest_claim: (implicit, via w6-* reports) sanitized ASan/UBSan/LSan native evidence
claims_exceeding_executed_evidence.finding: No workspace test compiles any CT fixture with -fsanitize. native_fault_run uses '-std=c11 -pthread -Wall -Wextra -Werror' only. The sanitizer evidence is a transcript pasted into the report (docs/reports/w6-*/README.md), re-run by no gate. The only sanitized C in the workspace (crates/qcore-core/tests/unit/c_emit.rs) runs a different, sequential corpus.
claims_exceeding_executed_evidence.severity: recorded evidence presented alongside gated evidence; regressions would not be caught
claims_exceeding_executed_evidence.proposed_repair: add a `native_sanitized` stage whose only legal values are "executed" (a real gate) or "recorded_not_gated" (transcript pointer)

claims_exceeding_executed_evidence.subject: CT02
claims_exceeding_executed_evidence.manifest_claim: semantic_profile: "CT01 supplies the accepted native control"
claims_exceeding_executed_evidence.finding: The link is narrative only. ct_corpus.rs:260-264 asserts expected.positive_control.is_some() == (case.id == "CT19"), so CT02 is structurally forbidden from carrying a control. Nothing in the harness ties CT02's rejection to CT01's acceptance; if CT01 were retired, CT02's claim would silently become false.
claims_exceeding_executed_evidence.proposed_repair: add a machine-checked `control_for`/`controlled_by` edge between cases and assert it in the harness

claims_exceeding_executed_evidence.subject: CT19
claims_exceeding_executed_evidence.finding: run_positive_control DOES execute a Linux-gated task reference execution on joined_sibling.qcore (root outcome 42, 2 children, both joined). That executed evidence is recorded nowhere in the manifest, and the case carries no evidence_target even though its control is Linux-gated. The control is never compiled or run natively.
claims_exceeding_executed_evidence.severity: under-records executed control evidence; target metadata missing
claims_exceeding_executed_evidence.proposed_repair: record control evidence as its own stage entry with its own artifact and host_gate

claims_exceeding_executed_evidence.subject: docs/reviews/r0_3/acceptance.json
claims_exceeding_executed_evidence.finding: acceptance.json carries NO per-CT rows at all -- only these two scalars. The scalar treats CT02 (source rejection, zero native runs) and CT16 (4 reference executions + 4 native runs) as one unit of coverage, and hides that 0 of 11 cases have proof evidence and 0 of 11 have gated sanitized-native evidence. R02 and R04 cite the w6-* reports and state their boundaries accurately in prose; the defect is that the consumable numbers are binary.
claims_exceeding_executed_evidence.severity: dashboard scalar exceeds executed stage evidence in depth, not in count
claims_exceeding_executed_evidence.proposed_repair: derive per-CT rows and a stage histogram from coverage.json instead of hand-maintaining two scalars

claims_exceeding_executed_evidence.subject: all 11 mapped cases
claims_exceeding_executed_evidence.finding: Correct and not an overclaim -- recorded here because it is the largest uniform gap. No Lean theorem is bound to any CT fixture; the only CT string in proof/ is a comment at proof/QCore/TaskExecution.lean:539 naming CT13. The task theorems constrain the Lean model, and source/native refinement is an explicit premise in every w6 report.
claims_exceeding_executed_evidence.proposed_repair: either bind theorems to fixtures via a checked mapping, or keep `unassessed` and stop citing Lean counts adjacent to CT counts

claims_exceeding_executed_evidence.subject: CT14, CT37
claims_exceeding_executed_evidence.manifest_claim: fixture inventory equals executed inputs (asserted at ct_corpus.rs:319)
claims_exceeding_executed_evidence.finding: Both fixtures' completion_before_join.h is a 66-byte one-line #include of compiler/tests/fixtures/task_worker_allocations/completion_before_join.h. The inventory assertion covers the stub, not the adapter that actually forces worker completion before creation returns. The shared adapter is outside the CT fixture tree and outside the inventory check.
claims_exceeding_executed_evidence.severity: provenance gap in an otherwise closed inventory check
claims_exceeding_executed_evidence.proposed_repair: record transitively included adapters as declared fixture inputs

missing_stage_tasks.title: CT02: native negative-control stage
missing_stage_tasks.detail: CT02 executes parse -> elaborate -> task_lowering -> task_ledger_check and stops at Q600. Its claimed accepted native control (CT01) is narrative. Add a harness-checked control edge so CT02's rejection is paired with an executed accepting run of the same shape, and so retiring CT01 breaks CT02 loudly.

missing_stage_tasks.title: CT19: native control stage and target metadata
missing_stage_tasks.detail: run_positive_control stops at task reference execution. Compile and run joined_sibling.qcore natively (as every other Linux case does) and record the control as its own stage entry with host_gate=[linux].

missing_stage_tasks.title: Sanitized-native stage as a real gate
missing_stage_tasks.detail: Promote the five w6 report transcripts into executing runs: compile the same emitted C with -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-omit-frame-pointer and LSan, as an opt-in gate (env-selected so the default suite stays fast) that fails rather than skips when selected. Until then the manifest must say recorded_not_gated.

missing_stage_tasks.title: Split the `cfg` and `type_checker` stage names
missing_stage_tasks.detail: Replace `cfg` (unevidenced, ambiguous) and the overloaded `type_checker` with the four stages the pipeline actually has. Mark sequential_whole_program not_applicable for every current mapped case and say so, rather than letting `cfg: executed` imply the sequential resource CFG ran.

missing_stage_tasks.title: Host-gated stage status
missing_stage_tasks.detail: Make the Linux scoping machine-readable so a non-Linux CI run reports unexecuted instead of inheriting `executed`.

missing_stage_tasks.title: Record the executed CLI end-to-end stage
missing_stage_tasks.detail: crates/qcorec/tests/cli.rs runs qcorec check + emit + clang + execute on CT01/case.qcore and CT13's fixture, and crates/qcore-frontend/tests/owned_tasks.rs runs ~25 adversarial mutations of CT01/case.qcore. This is executed evidence the manifest does not know about -- the only two cases with process-level end-to-end evidence.

missing_stage_tasks.title: Proof stage: bind or stop implying
missing_stage_tasks.detail: 0 of 11 cases have proof evidence and nothing links a Lean theorem to a fixture. Either add a checked fixture->theorem mapping, or keep `unassessed` and keep Lean audit counts out of CT coverage statements.

missing_stage_tasks.title: Declare transitively included native adapters
missing_stage_tasks.detail: The inventory assertion covers a 66-byte #include stub, not the shared adapter it pulls in from outside the CT tree.

missing_stage_tasks.title: Derive CT rows from stage evidence

proposed_manifest_schema.rationale: schema_version 1 records one flat status string per stage, derived in ct_corpus.rs from the fixture's verdict MODE rather than from observed execution. Two cases that stop at very different depths (a Q013 name error and a Q600 ledger rejection) are indistinguishable, and a Linux-gated stage reads 'executed' on every host.

stage_vocabulary.name: task_lowering
stage_vocabulary.note: lower_source_tasks; replaces part of the overloaded type_checker

stage_vocabulary.name: sequential_whole_program
stage_vocabulary.note: check_whole_program; not_applicable for every current mapped case

stage_vocabulary.name: legacy_c_twin
stage_vocabulary.note: reserved for CT40-CT43/CT45; does not exist yet

stage_vocabulary.name: proof
stage_vocabulary.note: a checked fixture->theorem binding; none exists

status_vocabulary.executed: a named executor ran this stage on this case's artifact AND fails if the stage's work is removed
status_vocabulary.unexecuted: the stage applies to this case but no executor runs it
status_vocabulary.recorded_not_gated: evidence exists as a transcript in a report; no gate re-runs it. Requires `record`
status_vocabulary.not_applicable: this case's mode cannot reach the stage (e.g. native_execution for a Reject case)

per_stage_fields.artifact: required when status==executed; the exact file executed
per_stage_fields.host_gate: optional list; when present the stage is executed only on those hosts
per_stage_fields.observations: optional count of distinct executed runs (scenarios, scripts, fault modes)
per_stage_fields.record: required when status==recorded_not_gated; path to the transcript

case_fields.controlled_by: optional list of case ids whose accepted execution is this reject case's control; harness-asserted (repairs O5)
case_fields.controls_recorded_separately: optional list of in-case rejection controls with their diagnostics

fail_closed_rules: status==executed without an executor or artifact is a harness failure
status==recorded_not_gated without a record is a harness failure
a mapped case with zero executed stages beyond parse is a harness failure
the executor set named across all cases must equal the harness's own registry of runners (extends the existing MAPPED_CASES pin)
an unknown stage name or status is a harness failure (preserves current deny_unknown_fields behavior)

summarizer_derivation.principle: counts are derived from executed stage evidence, never from mapping_status alone

outputs.name: ct_stage_histogram
outputs.how: for each stage name, count cases by status, evaluated for the reporting host
outputs.example_today: native_execution: executed 9 (linux) / not_applicable 2 / unexecuted 0; proof: unassessed 11

outputs.name: ct_depth_profile
outputs.how: bucket each mapped case by its deepest executed stage
outputs.example_today: source_reject 2 (CT02, CT19); native 9; native_sanitized 0 (5 recorded_not_gated); proved 0

outputs.name: ct_observation_counts
outputs.example_today: task_reference_execution 18; native_execution 19; in-case source rejection controls 11

outputs.name: ct_mapped
outputs.how: retained as count(mapping_status==mapped) but emitted ONLY alongside the histogram and an explicit note that mapping is not conformance

outputs.name: ct_host_scope

summarizer_derivation.acceptance_json_change: replace the hand-maintained ct_mapped/ct_unmapped scalars with generated per-CT rows plus the histogram and depth profile; a row may not claim depth its stage evidence does not carry (repairs O7)
summarizer_derivation.refusal: the summarizer emits no counts at all if any fail_closed_rule is violated
